Author: Gautam Chowdhary
Bench: Gautam Chowdhary
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:109365
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 1678 of 2024
Revisionist :- Prashant Kumar
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Revisionist :- Sushil Dubey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kuldeep Kumar
Hon'ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.
1.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On 23.05.2024, the following order was passed by this Court.

"1. On 22.04.2024, this Court had passed the following orders:-
1. Heard learned counsel for the revisionist, Sri Kuldeep Kumar, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The present revision has been filed for quashing the Judgement and order dated 09.02.2024 passed by learned Additional Principal Judge, Family Court No.01,
District Bulandshahr in Maintenance Case No. 775 of 2019 (Smt. Himani and another Vs. Prashant Kumar) under Section 125 Cr.P.C. whereby the application under Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75975134/
1 Section 125 Cr.P.C. filed by the opposite party no.2 has been allowed and the revisionist has been directed to pay maintenance of Rs. 20,000/- per month and Rs.
8000/- per month to the opposite party nos. 2 and 3.
3.

entities.text: Himani and another Vs. Prashant Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the very outset, learned counsel for the revisionist submit that the revisionist is ready to settle the matter and some date may be fixed on which date, the revisionist as well as opposite party no.2 may appear before this Court for amicable settlement between the parties.

4. Sri Kuldeep Kumar, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 submits that the maintenance of Rs. 28000/- has been directed to be paid to the opposite party nos. 2 and 3 from the date of filing application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. and till date more than 10 lacs is due to be paid by the revisionist to the opposite party nos. 2 and 3.

He further submits that he has no objection with regard to amicable settlement between the parties but to show bonafide, the revisionist deposit some amount and also to pay the expenses amount to the opposite party no.2 for her appearance before this Hon'ble Court.

5. Learned counsel for the revisionist further submits that the revisionist is ready to pay Rs. 6,00,000/- out of the due amount/arrears of the maintenance amount as has been awarded under Section 125 Cr.P.C. provided some relaxation may be granted to be deposited in equal monthly instalments.
He also agrees to pay monthly maintenance amount to opposite party no.2 as awarded, vide impugned Judgement and order.
He further submits that in case, the final settlement arrived between the parties, the amount already paid by the revisionist may be adjusted.
He further submits that in case the parties do not arrive at a settlement then in that case, the revisionist shall pay the remaining instalments as well as month to month instalment.

6. Considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the revisionist as well as facts and circumstances of the case, it is directed that the revisionist shall deposit Rs. 6,00,000/- (six lacs) towards the arrears of maintenance as on date, in three equal monthly installments before the concerned Court below.
The first installment shall be paid on or before 22.05.2024, the remaining two installments shall be paid by the revisionist on or before 22.06.2024, 22.07.2024 respectively.
Apart from the aforesaid, the revisionist shall also continue to pay monthly maintenance as awarded by the Court below by 07th of each calender month starting from June, 2024.
7. The amount so deposited by the revisionist shall be paid over to the opposite party no.2 after due verification by the concerned Court.

8. In case, the revisionist deposits the aforesaid amount within the aforesaid period,
no coercive action shall be taken against him.

Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75975134/
2

entities.text: Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, list this matter on 23.05.2024 for further hearing on which date the revisionist Prashant Kumar and the opposite party no.2 Smt. Himani shall remain present before this Court for amicable settlement between them.
The revisionist is further directed to bring on record the deposit receipt of first instalment by means of filing compliance affidavit.
Apart from the same, the revisionist shall also pay a sum of Rs. 20,000/- to the opposite party no.2 as expenses for her appearance before this Court.

10. It is made clear that in case, the parties do not arrive at any settlement, then the remaining instalments as well as monthly instalment as stated in paragraph no.6 of the instant order shall continue to be paid by the revisionist.

However, in case, the revisionist fails to deposit the aforesaid amount within a month from today or fails to deposit monthly maintenance amount as stipulated above, the protection granted by this Court shall automatically stand vacated and the Court below will be at liberty to proceed against the revisionist in accordance with law.

2. Pursuant to the earlier order of this Court dated 22.04.2024, the revisionist Prashant Kumar as well as opposite party no.2 Smt. Himani are present before this Court, who are identified by their respective counsel.

3. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that pursuant to the earlier order of this Court dated 22.04.2024, the revisionist had deposited the Ist instalment of Rs. 2 lacs vide draft no. 582433 before the concerned Family Court.

He further submits that the amount of Rs. 20,000/- as expenses, for appearance of the opposite party no.2 has also been deposited by the revisionist before the concerned Family Court, instead of paying the same before this Court and both the amount has been received by the opposite party no.2.
4. The aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the revisionist has not been rebutted by the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2.
5. Today, the revisionist as well as opposite party no.2 are present for amicable settlement between the parties.

6. The revisionist as well as opposite party no.2 have decided to live separately on payment of permanent alimony of Rs. 30 lacs by the revisionist to the opposite party no.2 in two equal instalments.

The revisionist has stated that the first instalment of Rs. 2 lacs as has been ordered by this Court vide order dated 22.04.2024 as well as Rs. 2 lacs which has also been paid by him pursuant to the order dated 09.11.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. (482) Application No. 37059 of 2023 may be adjusted towards the final settled amount.
The opposite party no.2 has no objection towards the adjustment of Rs. 4 lacs which has already been received by her.
The statements of the revisionist as well as opposite party no.2 have been recorded separately on a plain paper and has been kept as part of record.

Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75975134/
3 7.

entities.text: Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After deducting the amount of Rs. 4 lacs already paid by the revisionist to the opposite party no.2 out of the permanent alimony of Rs. 30 lacs, Rs. 26 lacs shall be paid by the revisionist to the opposite party no.2 in two equal instalments.
The first instalment shall be paid by the revisionist on or before 24.06.2024 before the concerned Family Court.

After depositing the first instalment,
petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act shall be filed by the parties between 01.07.2024 to 07.07.2024.

The second instalment of Rs. 13 lacs shall be paid by the revisionist on or before 24.08.2024 and the concerned Family Court shall proceed in accordance with law and will decide the case under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of four months from the date of filing such application.
8. The amount deposited by the revisionist shall be paid over to the opposite party no.2 after due verification by the concerned Court below.

9. It goes without saying t hat after filing of the joint petition under Section 13-B of of the Hindu Marriage Act, the opposite party no.2 shall also move an appropriate application before the concerned trial Court with respect to withdrawing of the cases filed by her against the revisionist under Section 498A I.P.C. along with other allied Section, under Domestic Violence Act pending between the parties.
10.
List this matter for further hearing on 22.07.2024 in the additional cause list on which date, the learned counsel for the revisionist shall file affidavit of compliance.

11. The revisionist as well as opposite party no.2 need not to appear before this Court in-person,
unless otherwise directed by this Court in future."
2.

Sri Sushil Dubey, learned counsel for the revisionist submits that pursuant to the order dated 23.05.2024, the revisionist had deposited Ist instalment of Rs. 13 lac, which was released in favour of the opposite party no.2 thereafter, a joint petition under petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act was filed.

The revisionist had also deposited the second instalment of Rs. 13 lacs before the Family Court pursuant to the direction issued by this Court on 23.05.2024 but before the final decision to be taken on the joint petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act, the revisionist Prashant Kumar died on 14.11.2024 and therefore, the present revision abate and prays to dismiss the same as abated.

3. Sri Rahul Kumar, learned counsel holding brief of Sri Kuldeep Kumar learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 could not dispute the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the revisionist, however he submits that since the matter was amicably settled by this Court on payment of permanent alimony of Rs. 26 lacs out of which the Ist instalment has already been withdrawn by the opposite party no.2.

He further submits that this Court had directed to release the second instalment in favour of the opposite party no.2 after decision on the petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act in the meantime, the revisionist died and that petition has also become infructuous, therefore the second instalment which is lying deposited in favour of the opposite party no.2 before the learned Family Court, after the decision on the joint petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act may be directed to be released in favour of the opposite party no.2.
Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75975134/
4 4.

entities.text: Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and after perusing the averments made in the present revision, this Court is of the opinion that since the revisionist and the opposite party no.2 had amicably settled their dispute and had decided to live separately on payment of permanent alimony of Rs. 26 lacs.

Out of which, Rs. 13 lacs has already been received by the opposite party no.2 and remaining 13 lacs was also deposited by the revisionist, which was directed to be released after decision on the petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act

, in the meantime, the revisionist died but that amount of Rs. 13 lacs towards the IInd instalment deposited before the concerned Family Court is liable to be released in favour of the opposite party no.2.

5. In view of the statement of learned counsel for the revisionist that the revisionist died, therefore,
the present revision abates.
6. Accordingly, it is dismissed as abated.
7. The concerned Family Court is directed to release the IInd instalment deposited by the revisionist in favour of the opposite party no.2 towards the permanent alimony, within a month from today.

Order Date :- 9.7.2025 S.Ali  Prashant Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75975134/
